Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a widened superior mediastinum with bilateral paratracheal fullness that is more prominent on the right side, causing deviation of the trachea to the left. This finding is consistent with bilateral paratracheal lymphadenopathy (often seen in conditions like tuberculosis or lymphoma) exerting a mass effect, rather than lung collapse or pleural effusion which would present with different radiographic signs.
